message.content: Stream fast: review the server package.

content.text:
I will review the server package from the top, starting with how the routes are registered and how each handler decodes its request body.
The plan, in order:
the mux, the decode helper, then the SSE writer, which is where most of the subtle bugs hide in a server like this one.

The handlers share one mux, and every one of them decodes its body with the same helper, so a malformed request gets the same plain error everywhere in the package. That is good, because the web app can rely on one error shape instead of guessing. Next I want to see whether the streaming handlers flush after each event.

The SSE writer flushes after every event and stops when the request context ends, which is exactly what a long running run needs. One thing is worth a second look: the writer does not set a write deadline, so a client that stops reading could hold a goroutine until the run ends! Let me check how the other handlers deal with slow readers.

None of the other handlers set a deadline either, and the server itself sets no WriteTimeout, so this is a package wide choice and not a slip in one file. Is that safe for a sidecar that only the local app talks to? I think it is, because the only reader is the app on the same machine, but I want the tests to say so.

The error handling is next, and here the package is just as even: a failed decode, a missing thread and a bot that does not exist all return the same small JSON error with a plain message and a status code that matches the problem. That is the shape the web app already expects, so there is nothing to change there, and the helper that writes it is only a few lines long.

The tests cover the happy path of every route and the error shape of the decode helper, but nothing exercises a client that disconnects in the middle of a stream. I would add one table case for that, since the code already handles it and the case would pin the behaviour down. Everything else in the package reads clearly and stays inside its layer.
The server package is consistent: one mux, one decode helper and an SSE writer that flushes after every event. One test for a client that disconnects mid stream is the only change worth making.

result: The server package is consistent: one mux, one decode helper and an SSE writer that flushes after every event. One test for a client that disconnects mid stream is the only change worth making.
